_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (nothing downloaded): frames every 3-15 s with 0.5 s bursts at 82 s and 445 s, words from the transcript panel, sound from the yt-style probe at 52-117 s. Our own descriptions; shots approximate. A stitched mid-roll ad covered ~200-295 s in our player, so that stretch is from the transcript and chapters only. Silicon Up Close, 1.02M views, 12.7K subs.

lines.gist: Your last AI question went through a chip with galaxy-many switches
The answer felt instant; we will follow the question all the way down
Map of the descent: memory, copper streets, one switch, its atoms
The question becomes numbers, radio, then light in a hair-thin fibre
It lands at a giant data-centre campus measured in fields and gigawatts
One cabinet, drawers of chips, cooled by liquid hotter than a hot tub
Two stamp-sized slabs hold as many switches as stars in the galaxy
Memory towers of stacked, thinned chips forget and refresh constantly
Flip the slab: a city of wiring, scaled up to the size of Manhattan
One switch like a cathedral; yes or no, billions of times, builds the answer
How small: blood cell, DNA, atoms you could count, electrons leaking
Climb back out, total the switches, answer returns as light; echoes the opening

ending.cta: asks viewers to comment what they asked

whyItWorks: One continuous descent (a powers-of-ten zoom) is the spine; each chapter is one scale step deeper, so the open loop is what sits at the bottom.
Every huge figure is turned into a body or city scale (hair, blood cell, Manhattan, grains of sand) the moment it is spoken.
Restrained dark photoreal 3D, slow constant camera drift and small lower-left labels that fade in on the word; no captions, no clutter.
Ends by climbing back out and repeating the opening idea, so the film closes as a loop.
